claims.text: An HEA coating with a graded interfacial layer will bond more effectively to a Cu substrate than an HEA coating deposited directly on Cu.
The graded coating will preserve the HEA's wear resistance.
Cr can act as an adhesion-promoting element at a Cu/HEA interface.
Ti can act as an adhesion-promoting element at a Cu/HEA interface.
The initial Cu matrix has a clean, untreated surface.
Magnetron sputtering followed by controlled thermal treatment can produce a graded transition from Cu to the bulk HEA.
Chemical compatibility at the coating/substrate interface is critical under high-friction and high-wear service conditions.
Mechanical integrity at the coating/substrate interface is critical under high-friction and high-wear service conditions.
A graded compositional interlayer reduces chemical-property mismatch at the Cu/HEA interface.
A graded compositional interlayer reduces mechanical-property mismatch at the Cu/HEA interface.
A gradual interfacial composition change enhances chemical compatibility between Cu and the HEA.
A gradual interfacial composition change minimizes thermal and mechanical stress concentrations.
Enhanced chemical compatibility and reduced stress concentrations improve bonding between the Cu substrate and the HEA.
The graded coating will provide significantly improved adhesion to Cu.
The graded coating will maintain or possibly enhance wear resistance under high-stress service conditions.
Conventional HEA coatings directly applied to Cu typically have poor interfacial adhesion.
The poor adhesion of conventional HEA coatings on Cu is caused by chemical and mechanical mismatches.
The effectiveness of the graded layer depends on its composition.
The effectiveness of the graded layer depends on its thickness.
The effectiveness of the graded layer depends on thermal-treatment parameters.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis only requires wear resistance to be preserved, and the predicted outcome allows it to be merely maintained, but the falsification rule requires a statistically significant improvement in both adhesion and wear resistance. Thus, an outcome with improved adhesion and unchanged wear resistance would satisfy the stated hypothesis but be classified as falsifying it.
